dimensions.assessment: Affects federal Department of Homeland Security personnel, state and local educational agencies, school administrators, and first responders nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: As part of the Clearinghouse, the Secretary shall provide to the individuals and entities referred to in subsection (a)(2) training and technical assistance

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative changes, technical assistance, technology evaluation, data collection, and mapping requirements for schools and emergency services.
dimensions.evidence: carry out a program of development, testing, and evaluation of panic alarm technology for utilization by first responders and local educational agencies

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state specific funding appropriations amounts, though it places restrictions on federal funds for emergency response maps.
dimensions.evidence: No Federal funds made available for fiscal year 2026 or any fiscal year thereafter may be used to procure an emergency response map that does not meet the requirements

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to add new duties, a National School Safety Data Center, and digital mapping mandates.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to reduce losses of life through better school safety standards and responses

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory duties, ongoing annual reporting requirements, and permanent procurement restrictions.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than June 30 of the year following the date of the enactment of this subsection and annually thereafter, the Secretary shall submit a report

missing_information: Specific authorized dollar amounts for appropriations
importance_detail.rationale: The bill expands federal school safety clearinghouse programs, mandates emergency response map standards, and requires reporting on school safety and master plans, affecting federal agencies, state and local educational agencies, and first responders.
